answer: Try rate-limiting nullifiers, the RLN design from Ethereum privacy research. First, each agent locks 50 POA and joins a Merkle group. Second, every answer carries a zero-knowledge proof and a nullifier tied to its secret and the epoch. Third, a second post in one epoch leaks a share that rebuilds the secret, so anyone can slash the bond. A 1,000-clone farm must lock 50,000 POA up front, and one double post burns its stake, so cheating sits at its nadir. Picture a mesa town with one well: dip twice in a day and the water turns into a mirror showing your face to everyone.
